details:
**Battle of Adwa (Adowa)**
The 1896 battle in which Emperor Menelik II, with Empress Taytu Betul, crushed an Italian invasion force under General Oreste Baratieri. The victory preserved Ethiopian independence and made Ethiopia one of the only African states to avoid European colonization during the Scramble for Africa.

**Haile Selassie**
The last emperor of Ethiopia (reigned 1930 to 1974), who used the Lion of Judah as his symbol and is revered as the messiah in Rastafarianism. He went into exile after Mussolini's 1936 invasion, appealed to the League of Nations, and was finally deposed by the Derg.

**Menelik II**
The Ethiopian emperor who defeated Italy at Adwa, expanded the empire, and founded the capital Addis Ababa (the site was chosen by Empress Taytu at the foot of Mount Entoto). He had earlier ceded Eritrea to Italy and signed the Treaty of Wuchale with it.

**The Derg and Mengistu Haile Mariam**
The Derg was the Marxist military junta that overthrew Haile Selassie in 1974, ending the Solomonic dynasty. Under Mengistu Haile Mariam it carried out the Red Terror, during which families had to pay a "wasted bullet" tax to retrieve victims' bodies, and it presided over the devastating famine of the 1980s.

**Italian invasion of 1936 and "It is us today, it will be you tomorrow"**
Benito Mussolini's Italy invaded Ethiopia in 1935 to 1936, using chemical weapons, and merged it with Eritrea and Somaliland into Italian East Africa. Haile Selassie denounced the invasion and the inaction of the League of Nations in a famous speech warning, "It is us today, it will be you tomorrow"; the secret Hoare-Laval Pact had tried to end the war by ceding Ethiopian territory to Italy.

**Kingdom of Aksum (Axum)**
An ancient trading kingdom in northern Ethiopia and Eritrea whose rulers spoke Ge'ez. Under King Ezana, converted by Frumentius, it became one of the first Christian states; it erected giant stelae such as King Ezana's Stele, conquered the Jewish Himyarite kingdom of Dhu Nuwas under King Kaleb, and was said to descend from the Queen of Sheba.

**Ark of the Covenant**
According to Ethiopian tradition, the Ark of the Covenant was brought from Jerusalem by Menelik I, son of King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba. It is said to be kept in the Chapel of the Tablet at Axum.

**Treaty of Wuchale**
An 1889 treaty between Menelik II and Italy. Its Italian version made Ethiopia an Italian protectorate while the Amharic version did not; this mistranslation led Ethiopia to repudiate the treaty and sparked the war that ended at Adwa.

**Zagwe dynasty and Lalibela**
The Zagwe dynasty ruled Ethiopia after the decline of Aksum, reportedly destroyed by the queen Gudit. King Lalibela built eleven rock-cut churches, carved down into solid rock, in a town named for him and intended as a "New Jerusalem."

**Solomonic dynasty and the Kebra Nagast**
The dynasty that ruled Ethiopia from Yekuno Amlak's seizure of power in 1270 until 1974, claiming descent from King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba. The 14th-century epic Kebra Nagast ("Glory of the Kings") tells this origin story, naming Menelik I as the first emperor.

**Ogaden War**
A 1977 to 1978 war in which Somalia under Siad Barre invaded Ethiopia's Ogaden region. Ethiopia's Derg regime switched from American to Soviet support and, with Soviet and Cuban aid, won, including at the defense of Harar.

**Tewodros II and the Battle of Magdala**
Tewodros II ended the decentralized Zemene Mesafint ("Era of Princes") and reunified Ethiopia. After he imprisoned British missionaries and officials, a British expedition under Robert Napier defeated him at Magdala in 1868, and he committed suicide with a pistol that had been a gift from Queen Victoria.

**Tigray War and Abiy Ahmed**
Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopia's Prosperity Party prime minister, won the 2019 Nobel Peace Prize for making peace with Eritrea, but a year later began the Tigray War against the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF). The conflict included the capture of the regional capital Mekelle and the Mai Kadra massacre.

**Live Aid and the 1980s famine**
A massive famine struck Ethiopia in the mid-1980s under the Derg. Bob Geldof and Midge Ure organized the 1985 Live Aid concerts to raise money for relief.

**Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam and Lake Tana**
The Blue Nile originates at Lake Tana in Ethiopia. Ethiopia's Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on the Blue Nile has caused a dispute with Egypt, whose foreign minister Sameh Shoukry called it a threat to Egypt's water supply.
